title: Apple Supplier Skyworks Soars After $2 Billion Stock Buyback Plan

organizations.name: skyworks shares of skyworks solutions inc.

text:
/ Markets Apple Supplier Skyworks Soars After $2 Billion Stock Buyback Plan Chipmaker Skyworks Solutions, a key Apple supplier, gives its stock a boost with the unveiling of plans for a $2 billion stock buyback program that will run through 2021. Feb6,20194:22PMEST Skyworks
Shares of Skyworks Solutions Inc. ( SWKS ) surged Wednesday even as the key supplier for Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) reported earnings that fell short of analysts' estimates amid a slowdown globally in mobile sales.
Skyworks price rose 11.5% to close at $84.69 in Wednesday trading after Skyworks' board gave the green light for a $2 billion stock buyback program that will run through 2021. That's double Skyworks' previous, $1 billion buyback program that just expired.
The Woburn, Mass.-based company, which provides Apple with mobile communications systems and radio frequency semiconductors, reported earnings of $1.83 a share, missing the $1.84 estimate of analysts surveyed by Zacks.
Skyworks fell short of Wall Street's expectations on revenue as well. The chipmaker reported revenue of $972 million for the quarter. That was down from $1.05 billion a year ago and 0.31% short of Zacks Consensus Estimate.
The decline in revenue comes as Skyworks major vendor, Apple, grapples with declining sales of iPhones in the Chinese market.
Liam Griffin, president and CEO of Skyworks, in a press statement pointed to a tougher market globally in the mobile business. He noted the company had cash flow of $500 million in the quarter that ended in December, with a stockpile of more than $1 billion in cash
"Despite macro weakness across our global mobile business, Skyworks delivered solid financial results driven by content gains, an expanding footprint in broad markets and our strong business model," Griffin said in a press release.
